In the drought, water cost 4.83× its earlier price with Law 5 and 4.75× without. The lowest room to pay of anyone was 0.05 days of the basic bundle a day with Law 5 and 0.08 without. The poorest tenth by holdings lived at 3.48 R a day in the drought with Law 5 and 5.07 without; by Aven output, 4.54 and 5.26. Owner-only dividends paid 0.00× their basic bundle at worst with Law 5, and 0.00× without. Person-days short: 545 with Law 5, 332 without.
experiments.takeaway: In the drought, dividends paid the owner-only blobs’ basics 0× over with Law 5 and not at all without it; 545 and 332 person-days were short.

experiments.question: Can a blob live without working?
experiments.ruleChanged: The owner-only cohort (5 %, Aven output 0, nothing held at the start) spends dividends and some of what it holds (base) vs dividends only (changed).
experiments.claim: Normal: never short from day 1. Strict: dividends alone pay the basic bundle by day 120, and the dividends-only cohort is never short after it.
experiments.evidence: normal short 142; dividends-only short 12349 (after day 120: 12271, last day 1094); strict test from day -1. On dividends only, the owner-only blobs were short 12349 person-days, the last on day 1094. Spending some of what they hold as well, they were short 142 person-days. Dividends alone paid every member’s bundle every day from day -1. Their living standard in the last year: 1.62 on dividends only, 5.05 normally.
experiments.takeaway: Living on dividends alone, the owner-only blobs went short until day 1094; spending some of what they hold as well, they were short on 142 person-days.

experiments.question: Where does the MIND end up?
experiments.ruleChanged: Treasuries pay their surplus above the 270-day reserve out for Aven work proposals (base) vs keep it (changed).
experiments.claim: Law 5 alone is not enough: with payout people hold most of the MIND, at least 20 points more than when treasuries keep their surplus.
experiments.evidence: people’s share 88.6 % (payout) vs 32.5 % (keep), gap 56.1 %. With payout, people held 88.6 % of all MIND at the end; when treasuries kept their surplus, 32.5 %. Treasuries held 4.8 % vs 61.2 %. The poorest decile lived at 8.33 with payout and 7.94 without.
experiments.takeaway: With payout, people ended up holding 89 % of all MIND; when treasuries kept their surplus, only 32 %.

experiments.question: Does inequality fade?
experiments.ruleChanged: Melt 7 % a year (base) vs 0 % (changed). In both worlds, holdings are made as unequal as Germany’s (Gini 0.72) at the start of year 9.
experiments.claim: The melt fades every advantage: with it, at least half the shock’s extra inequality is gone by the end, and the Gini ends lower than without the melt.
experiments.evidence: Gini 0.32 → 0.72 → 0.35 with melt; 0.35 → 0.72 → 0.40 without. The shock raised the Gini of holdings to 0.72. With the melt it fell to 0.35 by the end. Without the melt it fell to 0.40.
experiments.takeaway: After the shock the holdings Gini fell from 0.72 to 0.35 with the melt, and only to 0.40 without it.

experiments.question: What if a food COOP fails?
experiments.ruleChanged: Two food COOPs at genesis (base) vs one (changed). In both worlds the food COOP AGRI fails on day 300: its output drops to 10 % for a year.
experiments.claim: Two sellers of each basic keep everyone fed: with two food COOPs, nobody is short of food when one fails.
experiments.evidence: two food COOPs: 246 person-days short of food (the second seller was alive at the failure; receivership after 29 days); one: 256. With two food COOPs, people were short of food 246 person-days; with one, 256. The failing COOP went into receivership after 29 days (two sellers) and 29 days (one). The lowest food share anyone got was 52.9 % vs 50.4 %.
experiments.takeaway: When a food COOP failed, people were short of food on 246 person-days with two food COOPs and on 256 with one.

experiments.question: Can four friends cheat?
experiments.ruleChanged: Avens send HEARTS by delivered output per HEART (base) vs by the MIND’s pool price (changed). In both worlds, four friends open a COOP that makes nothing on day 365. They pay themselves 90 % of its treasury and buy its MIND to push its price.
experiments.claim: Avens that follow delivered output starve a ring: it gets less than under the price rule, and no more than its share of the people.
experiments.evidence: ring share of others’ HEARTS 0.2 % (output) vs 0.2 % (price); its share of people 1.3 %. Following delivered output, Avens sent the ring 0.2 % of others’ HEARTS; following the pool price, 0.2 %. The ring is 1.3 % of the people. Its members ended at 0.03× the others’ mean holding (output rule) and 0.03× (price rule).
experiments.takeaway: Avens that follow delivered output sent the ring 0.2 % of other people’s HEARTS; Avens that follow the pool price sent it 0.2 %.

experiments.question: Who keeps the surplus?
experiments.ruleChanged: Two competing COOPs per good at genesis (base) vs one (changed).
experiments.claim: When sellers compete, citizens win: with two sellers basics sell closer to cost, sellers keep less of the revenue, and nobody is short.
experiments.evidence: price ÷ full cost 1.14 (two) vs 1.10 (one); sellers’ share 74.7 % vs 74.2 %; short 545 vs 690. With two sellers per good, basics sold at 1.14× their full cost; with one, at 1.10×. Sellers kept 74.7 % vs 74.2 % of basics revenue above variable cost. The poorest decile lived at 6.62 vs 7.04.
experiments.takeaway: With two sellers per good, basics sold at 1.14× their full cost; with one seller, at 1.1×.

experiments.question: Which price rule feeds everyone?
experiments.ruleChanged: Forward-margin price with Mark-0’s guard (base) vs Primer’s adaptive price (changed): each seller asks 3 % more after a day it sold out, and 3 % less after a day with stock left.
experiments.claim: A price that reads need and the harvest pipeline feeds everyone: no one short, and no more shortage or price swing than Primer’s baseline.
experiments.evidence: short 545 (forward) vs 329,262 (Primer); daily swing 0.8 % vs 2.5 %. With the forward margin, 545 person-days were short; with Primer’s adaptive price, 329,262. Basics’ prices swung 0.8 % a day vs 2.5 %. The poorest decile lived at 6.62 vs 3.26.
experiments.takeaway: People were short on 545 person-days with the forward margin and 329,262 with Primer’s adaptive price, whose basics’ prices swung more from day to day.

experiments.question: Does more money make us richer?
experiments.ruleChanged: 24 (base) vs 48 (changed) HEARTS a day for every person. The Aven rate card is a number in R indexed to the HEARTS issued a day (HEARTS a day ÷ 24), so it doubles too. HEARTS never pay for goods.
experiments.claim: Doubling HEARTS changes only prices: real consumption of every good, and the mean living standard, within ±1 %. This holds because the Aven rate card (in R) is indexed to the HEARTS issued a day; with the card fixed in R it does not (the proof suite’s B28 reports that world).
experiments.evidence: largest change: compute -0.4 %; living standard -0.2 %; food 0.0 %, water -0.0 %, energy -0.0 %, bed 0.0 %, goods -0.0 %, spring 0.0 %, compute -0.4 %. With twice the HEARTS, food’s price in R went ×2.00, water’s ×2.00, energy’s ×2.00. What people got changed by at most 0.4 % for any good. The mean living standard changed by -0.2 %.
experiments.takeaway: With twice the HEARTS, food’s price in R went ×2 while what people got of any good changed by at most 0.4 %.

experiments.question: Does more energy make us richer?
experiments.ruleChanged: The geothermal stage and R&D on surplus energy on (base) vs both off (changed).
experiments.claim: Living standards (mean and poorest decile) end higher with surplus energy and R&D than without, and recipes get better only with it.
experiments.evidence: mean 8.33 vs 4.07; poorest decile 8.33 vs 1.49; recipes 61.7 % vs 0.0 % of the way to their physical best. With geothermal and R&D, a person used 90.30 kWh a day in the last year, 77.08 kWh were exported for accelerators and 7.82 kWh were surplus (R&D, storage, curtailed); R&D took 106,645 MWh over the run (recipes 61.7 % of the way to their physical best). Without, 38.45 kWh used, 45.42 exported, and 0.0 %. The poorest decile went from 5.16 to 8.33 with surplus energy, and from 4.87 to 1.49 without. Person-days short: 545 vs 727,564.
experiments.takeaway: With geothermal and R&D the poorest tenth went from 5.16 to 8.33 R a day; without them, from 4.87 to 1.49.

experiments.question: What stops a small village first?
experiments.ruleChanged: 1,500 blobs (base) vs 600 blobs (changed) in the same village, built for 1,500, with dome solar and no geothermal stage yet (world model 5.5). This experiment changes the population.
experiments.claim: Physics, not money, sets the limit: MIND never binds a basic while physics allows need, and fewer people on the same hex are short less.
experiments.evidence: MIND-bound basic day-goods 579 (1,500) and 87 (600); person-days short of a basic 92,540 (1,500) and 637 (600); days short a person 61.69 vs 1.06; short days by limit (1,500): {"food: MIND":233,"water: MIND":263,"energy: not built (free land, no project)":34,"energy: MIND":199,"bed: MIND":192,"bed: not built (free land, no project)":71,"bed: energy":31}. With 1,500 blobs, someone was short of energy on 233 days and of water on 263. With 600, on 29 and 29 days. MIND bound a basic on 579 day-goods with 1,500 and 87 with 600. Wood was bound by demand (1,500) and demand (600).
experiments.takeaway: With 1,500 blobs, 92,540 person-days were short of a basic (61.69 days a person; someone short of energy on 233 days); with 600 in the same village, 637 person-days (1.06 a person; energy on 29 days). MIND bound a basic on 579 and 87 day-goods.

experiments.question: Do newcomers eat?
experiments.ruleChanged: A constant population (base) vs +2 % a year (changed), on the same fixed land. Newcomers arrive with an Aven and nothing held.
experiments.claim: Growth raises rent, not hunger: newcomers are never short, and ground rent ends higher than with a constant population.
experiments.evidence: newcomers short 0 of 41857 person-days; rent at the end 1.15e-5 (growth) vs 1.13e-5 (constant). With growth the village went from 1500 to 1584 people. Newcomers lived 41,857 person-days in their first three years and were short on 0. Ground rent went from 7.74e-5 to 1.15e-5 R a m² a day (constant population: 1.13e-5). The mean living standard ended at 8.28 vs 8.33.
experiments.takeaway: The village grew to 1584 people; newcomers were never short, and ground rent ended 1.02× the rent with a constant population.

experiments.question: Private land or City land?
experiments.ruleChanged: All land belongs to the City COOP and is leased for ground rent (base) vs land owned by people, unequally (a Pareto draw), with the rent paid to them (changed).
experiments.claim: Land that nobody can sell keeps ownership fairer: the holdings Gini ends lower with City land than with private land, and nobody is short.
experiments.evidence: Gini 0.32 (City) vs 0.34 (private); short 545 vs 617. With City land the holdings Gini ended at 0.32; with private land, at 0.34. The poorest decile lived at 8.33 vs 8.33, the top decile at 8.33 vs 8.33.
experiments.takeaway: The holdings Gini ended at 0.32 with City land and at 0.34 with private land.

experiments.question: What happens on day 1?
experiments.ruleChanged: The bootstrap on (base: each Aven’s first HEARTS go to the basics COOPs it buys from, and pools fill on day 0) vs off (changed: first HEARTS into three COOPs of the Aven’s taste).
experiments.claim: Seed the pools, and the first day feeds everyone: with the bootstrap nobody is short on day 0 or after.
experiments.evidence: bootstrap: 0.0 % short on day 0, 0 person-days in year 1; without: 1.0 % on day 0, 52,169 person-days. With the bootstrap, 0.0 % of people were short on day 0 and 0.0 % on day 1. Without it, 1.0 % and 1.0 %. Over year 1: 0 vs 52,169 person-days short.
experiments.takeaway: With the bootstrap nobody went short on day 0; without it, 1 % did.

experiments.question: Does doubling a binding physical limit raise living standards?
experiments.ruleChanged: The hot spring’s warm ponds are fixed by nature and bind every day: 2 sites (base) vs 4 (changed).
experiments.claim: Doubling the binding physical limit raises living standards: more of the good, a higher mean living standard and a higher one for the poorest decile.
experiments.evidence: spring 1.11 → 1.11 h a person a day (badge “nature” on 95.4 % of base days), mean 7.05 → 7.06, poorest decile 6.62 → 6.72; capacity per person 8.16 → 9.05. Doubling the warm ponds took spring time from 1.11 to 1.11 hours a person a day, and its price from 1.50 to 0.30 R. The mean living standard went from 7.05 to 7.06 (0.1 %), the poorest decile’s from 6.62 to 6.72.
experiments.takeaway: Doubling the warm ponds took spring time from 1.11 to 1.11 hours a person a day and changed the mean living standard by 0.1 %.

experiments.question: What does the tower add, and what does it cost?
experiments.ruleChanged: The village without the Tower180 (base: one more Dome120 of utilities and community halls in the centre hex) vs with it (changed), at its real cost: the tower’s shell, floors and equipment on the founding bill, its beds, its solar cells, its halls’ upkeep, climate and heat.
experiments.claim: A comparison, not a test: what the tower adds (beds, solar) against what it costs (the founding bill, the imports to keep it up, its energy).
experiments.evidence: founding +€209 M; imports 39.8 % a year; electricity made 12.1 %; mean living standard 0.0 %. Founding bill €479 M without the tower, €688 M with it. Beds 1,740 vs 1,848; solar 60.02 vs 63.37 GWh a year. Electricity made 118.81 vs 133.19 kWh a person a day; exported 61.57 vs 55.00. Imports €54,068,833 vs €75,567,100 a year (materials €53,307,828 vs €74,500,750). Person-days short 545 vs 622; mean living standard 8.33 vs 8.33, poorest tenth 8.33 vs 8.33.
experiments.takeaway: The tower adds 108 beds and 3.35 GWh of solar a year for €209 M more at the founding; the mean living standard changes by 0.0 %.

experiments.question: Does selling Aven service abroad repay the bank?
experiments.ruleChanged: Electricity is the village’s only export (base) vs the MaiaCity COOP also buying Aven service from avenCEO in MIND and selling it abroad for euros (changed): at a sourced market price for an accelerator-hour (€2), bounded by a small provider’s demand (1,024 accelerators at 55 % use), only while the bank is behind and while an accelerator-hour abroad earns more than its electricity and its accelerator cost in euros.
experiments.claim: A comparison, not a test: what selling Aven service abroad does to the bank’s balance (the bootstrap number and the year the founding euros are back) and to the village’s own Aven service.
experiments.evidence: bootstrap €602.29 M → €601.57 M; repaid not in the run → not in the run; AI exports €1,418,274 a year; Aven help 0.0 %. Bootstrap number €602.29 M (electricity only) vs €601.57 M (with AI exports); cumulative balance at the end €-602.29 M vs €-601.57 M; exports less imports in the last 10 years €-2.68 M vs €-2.91 M a year; repaid in year never in the run vs never in the run. AI exports €1,418,274 a year; electricity exports €4,809,267 vs €4,714,212; accelerators imported €274,500 vs €1,592,000 a year; 42 vs 208 accelerators at the end. Aven help 24.00 vs 24.00 h a person a day, work 7.00 vs 6.56 h; person-days short 545 vs 352; mean living standard 8.32 vs 8.32, poorest tenth 8.07 vs 8.06.
experiments.takeaway: Selling Aven service abroad earned €1,418k a year; the bootstrap number went from €602.29 M to €601.57 M, and the bank is repaid never at the last decade’s pace (exports did not cover imports) (electricity only: never at the last decade’s pace (exports did not cover imports)).

experiments.question: Through a drought, a dark winter, two failing COOPs and a failing well, does everyone keep the basics, and does every decile recover within two years?
experiments.ruleChanged: No shocks (base) vs five scheduled shocks (changed): a drought (rain −50 %, summer of year 2), a dark winter (sun −60 %, winter of year 3), two COOPs’ output to 10 % for a year (WEST, the West settlement COOP selling beds, and GOODS-A, year 5), and the geothermal well down for 90 days (winter of year 6).
experiments.claim: Nobody is short in any shock, and every decile is back within two years (P3 holds with the shocks excused for two years).
experiments.evidence: short 167,458 person-days ({"food: MIND":117,"water: MIND":162,"energy: MIND":99,"energy: not built (free land, no project)":18,"bed: MIND":125,"bed: not built (free land, no project)":66,"bed: energy":45}); P3 fails (worst fall outside the windows 38.9 %; failing: holdings tenth 1, holdings tenth 2, holdings tenth 3, holdings tenth 4, holdings tenth 5, holdings tenth 6, holdings tenth 7, holdings tenth 8, holdings tenth 9, holdings tenth 10, aven tenth 1, aven tenth 2, aven tenth 3, aven tenth 4, aven tenth 5, aven tenth 6, aven tenth 7, aven tenth 8, aven tenth 9, aven tenth 10). Through the shocks, 167,458 person-days were short of a basic (545 without shocks). The largest fall of any decile outside the two-year recovery windows was 38.9 % (76.7 % without). The mean living standard ended at 7.73 vs 8.33. There were 8 receiverships vs 1.
experiments.takeaway: Through the five shocks people were short on 167,458 person-days, and not every tenth was back within two years.
